A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GODA research. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison, including material relocated into v2's Appendices A–C. v1 has no separately labelled appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original GODA data-quality measurements, policy evaluations, ablations and traffic-control simulation results, alongside some baseline results attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds visual-observation, DMG, online SAC, component-ablation and reward-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The original offline denoiser, loss and RTG/timestep conditioning remain unchanged. However, v2 adds a visual pipeline using BC pretraining, frozen encoders, latent-space augmentation and output-head fine-tuning (Section 4.1.2), plus an online procedure with periodic diffusion retraining, hybrid replay and changing goal schedules (Appendix C.2, Algorithm 2). These substantially extend the procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds Medium-Expert locomotion datasets, pixel-based V-D4RL Cheetah-Run at four data-quality levels, and online interaction scenarios for three Gym tasks. These expand represented data quality, observation modality and interaction conditions. The original Gym, Maze2D, Adroit and traffic-control coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The external augmentation baselines TATU, SynthER and DiffStitch remain unchanged in corresponding experiments. Table 6 adds four internal comparison variants removing either gated connection or only its gating, beyond v1's AdaLN/in-context comparisons. BC, DMG and SAC otherwise serve as new evaluation backbones using familiar unaugmented/SynthER controls.

E3.justification: Section 5 revises the reported diversity metric from L2 distance to average nearest-neighbor Min L2 Distance, with corresponding changes to Equation 11 and results. Added protocols include latent-space BC evaluation, DMG evaluation and online SAC over 100K interactions. The online experiment uses update-to-data ratios of 1 for vanilla SAC and 20 for both augmented methods, so that comparison has unequal update budgets.

E4.justification: v2 adds separate connection/gating ablations (Table 6), a reward-sensitivity investigation of Adroit failures (Appendix C.3, Table 10), and scaling-factor experiments across additional dataset-quality levels (Figure 10). These investigate component contributions and failure conditions beyond v1's analyses. Existing mixed-dataset and traffic-data-size studies are retained in Appendices C.5–C.6.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 adds weighted-least-squares reward-sensitivity estimation and 95th-percentile statistical summaries. These are diagnostic estimates, not confidence intervals. The principal benchmark's five-seed declaration and existing ± and error-band reporting practices remain unchanged; no increase in runs or new significance testing is documented.

E6.justification: Original task-level Gym/Maze2D, Adroit and traffic-control scores are retained, but v2 adds substantial results for the new settings and analyses. For example, visual BC averages are 39.9±4.8 with GODA versus 37.5±3.5 with SynthER (Table 4). The Gym IQL GODA average changes from 54.7 to 66.2 because Medium-Expert rows are added, not because retained task scores improve. Distance values also change under the revised metric.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 corrects v1's RTG-offset reasoning: adding a constant to every RTG changes the terminal reward, not the first reward. v2 also revises the distance definition and introduces a Lipschitz-based reward-sensitivity definition and composite measure in Appendix C.3. The central method equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain their central novelty and performance claims. Section 7 adds qualifications that GODA cannot synthesize expert-level performance from nonexpert data alone and requires latent representations for visual applications. These narrow the stated applicability without replacing the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations for return-prior superiority, dataset-dependent scaling benefits and Pen-Human failure, together with explicit expert-data and visual-input limitations. It also introduces a Maze2D explanation involving direct spatial-goal conditioning, although the documented conditioning remains RTG and timestep; this is an unsupported interpretive addition rather than an established input change.

D1.justification: v2 documents substantial implementation information for its extensions: 84×84×3 observations encoded into 50-dimensional representations, encoder freezing and head fine-tuning, and online augmentation of 1M samples per 10K interactions with a 1:1 real/synthetic ratio and changing goal parameters. Sensitivity-analysis procedures and weights are also supplied. Original denoiser hyperparameters, hardware and timing information are retained in Appendix B.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting visual offline RL, DMG, SAC and image-generation conditioning, and updates several introductory application citations. Its central positioning against SynthER and DiffStitch remains unchanged. Moving the largely retained related-work discussion to Appendix A is organizational rather than a substantive positioning change.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the paper, moving related work, implementation details and selected existing analyses into appendices. Method explanations expand to distinguish training from sampling, provide worked goal-selection examples and explain algorithm stages. Experimental sections are reorganized around the expanded evaluations, beyond routine wording edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout and substantially redistributes figures and tables. v2 adds a workflow diagram, goal-selection examples, new result tables and online/scaling plots, and redraws the diversity-distance panel. Several original ablation plots are retained unchanged but relocated; the mixed-dataset table's previously incorrect caption is corrected.

improvement.justification: Where v1 left individual gating contributions and the Pen-Human failure largely unexamined, v2 supplies component controls, sensitivity analysis and broader scaling tests. The explicit nearest-neighbor metric, clearer procedures and concrete applicability limits substantially improve scrutiny of the central claims. Unequal SAC update budgets and the unsupported spatial-goal explanation weaken parts of the added interpretation, but do not outweigh these gains.
